title: ClearPath Managed IT Services Service Desk Guide: Ticket Priority and Scope
content:
## Priority

The ClearPath Managed IT Services service desk assigns priority from impact and urgency:

| Priority | Meaning |
|---|---|
| P1 | A complete outage of a business-critical system, or a confirmed security incident, with no workaround |
| P2 | A business-critical system degraded, or an outage affecting a single site or department, with a workaround |
| P3 | A single user unable to work, or a non-critical system down |
| P4 | A service request, how-to question or scheduled change |

Where the tier requires phone reporting for P1, a ticket is worked and measured as P1 only when it was reported by phone. An outage reported through the portal, email or chat is logged as P2 until the client calls it in, and a phoned-in escalation is recorded as a reprioritisation at the moment of the call.

## Priority changes and the response guarantee

- When a ticket's priority is raised, the first-response guarantee of the new priority is measured from the moment of the reprioritisation.
- When it is lowered, the guarantee of the lower priority is measured from the original opening.
- A reprioritisation after the first response does not change the priority used for the service level.

## Scope

Scope is determined when the ticket is opened, from the tier's entitlements:
- help desk work is covered only where the tier includes covered remote help desk work in the seat fee;
- Microsoft 365 tenant administration only where the tier covers it;
- liaison with line-of-business vendors and the ISP only where the tier covers it;
- firewall, switch and wireless changes only where the tier covers network device changes;
- user onboarding and user offboarding tickets are covered wherever the tier includes covered remote help desk work.

Work outside those entitlements is billable out of scope. Any single change whose estimated effort exceeds 8 hours, new deployments, migrations and office moves are project referral and are quoted under a project statement of work instead of being billed as ticket labor.

## Account-team entitlements

Strategic reviews with the virtual CIO, the named client success manager, the technical account manager and security awareness training are entitlements of the tier and are scheduled through the account team, never billed as ticket labor.

## Hypothetical cases

- A portal report of a full email outage on a tier requiring phone reporting for P1 is logged P2; when the client phones it in, the ticket is raised to P1 and the P1 guarantee runs from that call.
- A request estimated at 10 hours for a single change is project referral; one estimated at 6 hours is ticket work, covered or billable according to the tier's entitlements.
